question: In iron deficiency anaemia (IDA), both serum ferritin and serum iron are low, whereas in anaemia of chronic disease (ACD), serum ferritin is elevated (or normal) and serum iron is low.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Review the iron study patterns. In IDA: low ferritin, low serum iron, HIGH TIBC (iron-hungry marrow). In ACD: normal-to-HIGH ferritin, low serum iron, LOW/normal TIBC. The hepcidin mechanism locks iron in macrophages in ACD.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. This is the key differentiator: in IDA, ferritin is depleted because iron stores are empty; in ACD, ferritin is an acute-phase reactant and rises despite functional iron restriction. TIBC is high in IDA and low/normal in ACD.
